entries.name: Uttar Pradesh's rolls read into tables
entries.covers: Four of Uttar Pradesh's rolls, one file for each of the 403 Assembly constituencies. They are the roll of the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the draft and final rolls of the intensive revision, and the draft roll of the 2027 summary revision. The first release came on 24 November 2026 and the second, which added 4,015 newer parts of the two rolls of the intensive revision, on 25 November.
entries.how: s1d labs says it read about 6.8 lakh of the Commission's PDFs, most of them scanned images, with five optical character readers and no language model. The 2027 roll, the only one of the four with a text layer, was read directly.
entries.access_text: The files it publishes replace names, relatives' names, EPIC numbers and house numbers with keyed-hash tokens, so that one elector can be followed from roll to roll and counted by age and gender. It sends the full text to journalists and researchers who apply.
entries.limits: It says the Commission's PDFs remain the authority and its counts are not official figures. Hand checks found every field right in 96.77 per cent of records of the intensive revision, from 402 boxes, and in 97.35 per cent of records on the 2024 roll. It says the tokens do not make a record anonymous. The figures here follow the README of the second release. The landing page, read on 25 November, still carried the first release's warning that newer parts were missing from the two rolls of the intensive revision and that its totals should not be compared with the official ones.
entries.recorded: Its counts leave out the entries with a deleted mark.

compare.what: Entries on the draft roll of the intensive revision
Entries on the final roll of the intensive revision

entries.name: Uttar Pradesh's final roll, constituency by constituency
entries.covers: Uttar Pradesh's rolls from the 2024 roll to the final roll, constituency by constituency, with the lists of names left off the draft of January 2026 by age and sex, and the errors on the final roll.
entries.how: Aman Bhargava of Diagram Chasing reads the rolls as digitised by s1d labs against the Chief Electoral Officer's totals.
entries.access_text: The findings are on a free page with charts and a table for every constituency. Its headline totals are the Chief Electoral Officer's, and its other counts are its own, from the digitised rolls.
entries.limits: The page says that some mistakes may have come in through character recognition, and that every example it shows and a random sample of each kind were checked by hand against the original documents.

entries.maker: Diagram Chasing, with Mathakaavalu and Edellu Karnataka
entries.name: Karnataka's final roll followed back to the 2002 roll
entries.covers: Karnataka's final roll of 27 October, joined to the 2002 roll, the January 2025 roll, the list of names left off the draft and the notice lists.
entries.how: Aman Bhargava read all 60,923 booth files of the final roll by machine and joined them by EPIC number to digitised copies of the older rolls and lists, which the groups Mathakaavalu and Edellu Karnataka made.
entries.access_text: The findings are on a free page. Aman Bhargava says there that an anonymised dataset of the final roll is on GitHub and that the version with names is shared for public-interest work on request, with no promise of approval. The older rolls and lists that Mathakaavalu and Edellu Karnataka digitised are not offered there.
entries.limits: He says his counts are minimums, that the rolls by themselves cannot establish identity, and that the work rests on optical character recognition of files the Commission publishes as PDFs.

compare.what: Names left off the draft that he found on the January 2025 roll

entries.name: Uttar Pradesh's rolls and Form 6 applications, counted
entries.covers: Three reports. One sets the draft roll of 6 January 2026 against the final roll of 10 April 2026 for 69 polling stations in 20 districts, covering 60,558 electors, with the published lists of Form 6 applications of 13 Assembly constituencies. One reads the whole draft roll of the summary revision of 17 November for parents listed with the same age as the elector or a younger one. One counts the Form 6 applications day by day from 29 October to 22 November.
entries.how: Alt News chose the 69 polling stations itself and counted two entries as the same person only where the name, the name of the father or husband, the age and the house number all matched. For the parents, it took every elector whose entry names a father or a mother and looked in the same polling station for an elector of that name living in the same house. For Form 6 it matched applicants by their name and the name of the father or husband within each constituency.
entries.access_text: The findings are in free reports with examples. Every count is Alt News's own.
entries.limits: Alt News says a shared or missing house number is in itself no evidence of irregularity, and that name changes between the rolls could be legitimate corrections that only the Form 8 applications can explain.
entries.recorded: Neither Alt News nor the Chief Electoral Officer says how its count of the applications was made.

official.who: The Chief Electoral Officer's statement of 24 November

entries.name: Uttar Pradesh's Form 7 disclosures
entries.covers: The more than 4.3 lakh Form 7 objections that Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer published on his website during the intensive revision.
entries.how: The Collective scraped the disclosures from the Chief Electoral Officer's website with a team of data analysts and counted the requests filed by registration officers and assistant registration officers, and those that gave no reason.
entries.access_text: The findings are in free reports. The disclosures themselves are on the Chief Electoral Officer's website.
entries.limits: The Collective says the published disclosures give no identity of an objector beyond a name, so the objectors cannot be checked.
entries.recorded: The Collective corrected its count of requests with no reason from 85,854 to 87,127 on 20 October. Before that, the Chief Electoral Officer's office called the claims misleading, IANS reported on 13 October 2026, and in a recorded video the Chief Electoral Officer did not dispute the count of 85,854, by the Collective's follow-up of 14 October.

entries.name: Uttar Pradesh's Form 6 applications
entries.covers: The Form 6 applications for inclusion that Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer published during the intensive revision, set against the electors added to the final roll.
entries.how: The Collective set the 71.38 lakh Form 6 applications the Chief Electoral Officer published against the 84.3 lakh electors added to the final roll, and traced the gap to 16.18 lakh applications taken before the draft, whose names and details were not published.
entries.access_text: The findings are in free reports.
entries.recorded: The Chief Electoral Officer confirmed that the 16.18 lakh applications were taken before the draft roll and said their details were withheld on the Commission's instructions, by the Collective's follow-up of 8 October. The New Indian Express reported that he rejected the first report on X.

compare.what: Electors added to the final roll, as the Collective gives it, against the rise from the draft to the final roll

entries.name: Pilibhit's booths, matched by EPIC number
entries.covers: The Commission's data for 55 of the 419 booths of Pilibhit, and 12,082 correction forms submitted across Uttar Pradesh between April and September 2026.
entries.how: The Collective matched entries in the Commission's data by EPIC number against the final roll of 10 April 2026, checked 15 of the cases on the ground against two government photo identity documents for each, and read the Commission's Form 8 manual and the code of the ECINET and ERONET apps.
entries.access_text: The findings are in a free report.
entries.limits: The Commission's disclosures of correction forms give only the voter's name and Assembly constituency and no EPIC number, which the Collective says makes it nearly impossible for the public to tell whose entry was changed.
entries.recorded: The Chief Electoral Officer's press note of 22 October said the computer assistant at the constituency's voter registration centre had entered 13,779 Form 8 applications between 31 May and 29 August 2026, with no form or record of any of them in the office. The Collective counted 2,691 entries changed at the 55 booths, and 2,638 of them still on the roll eight days after that finding.

entries.name: Rajasthan's list of the dead, set against the panchayat roll
entries.covers: Rajasthan's list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors from the intensive revision, and the State Election Commission's panchayat roll.
entries.how: The Collective compared the two by each elector's voter ID and EPIC number, after downloading both rolls in October, and checked a sample against the State Election Commission's own search portal.
entries.access_text: The findings are in a free report.
entries.limits: The Collective says it did not verify on the ground which of the two commissions is right, and that it could not check the Commission's monthly updates to the roll since the revision.

compare.what: Electors marked dead on the list

entries.name: Returning officers' reports of polling day, 2024
entries.covers: The Election Commission's internal reports of the returning officers for 530 Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies in Maharashtra, Haryana and Jammu and Kashmir that voted in 2024, and two reports for Chittoor in Andhra Pradesh. The series concerns polling-day records of the 2024 elections and does not cover the roll revisions.
entries.how: The Collective read the reports and counted those that carry no count of votes polled after 5 pm.
entries.access_text: The findings are in free reports in its Election Audit series.
entries.limits: The Collective says it does not conclude whether or where voting was rigged. For Chittoor it says it has so far reviewed the reports for only one parliamentary seat.
entries.recorded: The Chief Electoral Officers of Haryana, Jammu and Kashmir and Maharashtra answered that the Commission publishes the votes polled in its index cards, that the returning officer's report is a non-statutory summary and that no separate statutory record of polling after 5 pm exists. The Collective says it stands by its reporting.

entries.name: West Bengal's appeals before the tribunals
entries.covers: The appeals before West Bengal's appellate tribunals, against electors whom judicial officers cleared and by electors whom they deleted, by district, seat and booth.
entries.how: The group, which the Hindustan Times describes as a research collective based in Kolkata, compiled its statewide figures from the tribunals' appeal portal.
entries.access_text: It publishes a report on the tribunals with its counts. The Wire and the Hindustan Times reported from its records.
entries.limits: The group says the portal does not show the outcome of a disposed appeal.
entries.recorded: The Commission reported 16,10,311 appeals against inclusion to the Supreme Court in September, which The Wire set beside the group's count.

official.who: Election Commission, reply affidavit in the Supreme Court filed on 16 September 2026, paragraph 23

entries.name: A review of ECINET's code, and an audit of Form 6 data
entries.covers: The code ECINET serves to a browser before login, read on 2, 6, 7 and 9 October and in code fetched on 19 October, and the personal data voters submitted through Form 6 on the Commission's Citizen Service Portal.
entries.how: Saurav Rajput, a data scientist at the civic-tech initiative, reviewed the code ECINET serves publicly, with no passwords and no use of ECINET's programming interfaces. For Form 6, Charchagram says its verification found records going back to 2023.
entries.access_text: The findings reached the public through the Hindustan Times, The Hindu and The Wire, and Charchagram's own posts on X.
entries.limits: The review read only code a browser receives before login, so it cannot say whether a rule was ever used, whether the server enforces it, or when it was added.
entries.recorded: The Hindustan Times said it could not verify the review independently.

entries.name: The lists of names left off, state by state
entries.covers: Reports on the lists of names left off the draft in Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Delhi, Uttarakhand, Meghalaya and Manipur, a fact sheet on West Bengal from 91 lakh elector records, and a preliminary analysis of Telangana outside Hyderabad reported by Frontline.
entries.how: The Institute compiled the Election Commission's booth-wise lists of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors. Its Uttar Pradesh report says the roll does not record religion and that the Institute estimates it from the elector's and the relative's names with its own model.
entries.access_text: Each report is a free download. The report pages offer no download of the compiled lists.
entries.limits: The Uttar Pradesh report says that some of the people on the lists will have applied again and may appear on the final roll, and that correlation is not causation. The Maharashtra report says that none of its figures proves any group was targeted.
pages: Politicians and commentators set beside the official figures

compare.what: Names left off the draft with a recorded reason
Names on the lists, at least

entries.name: The Hindu's data desk on the lists and rolls
entries.covers: The Bihar electors left off the draft by reason, sex and age, the gender ratio of the rolls in the states where the revision began in November 2025, Maharashtra's draft roll of 31 August and the lists of names left off it, and Delhi's draft roll matched to the lists of those sent notices.
entries.how: For Delhi the paper read the draft roll of 97.54 lakh electors, matched it to the lists of the 33.12 lakh sent notices and guessed each elector's religion from their name and their relative's name.
entries.access_text: The pieces are for subscribers, and only their openings are free to read.
entries.limits: In the Delhi piece the religion of each elector is the paper's estimate from names.

entries.name: Rajasthan's names left off, set against the local body rolls
entries.covers: The electors left off Rajasthan's draft roll, 41.65 lakh by PUCL's count, set against the State Election Commission's rolls for the 2026 panchayat and urban local body elections, up to its second supplement to the panchayat rolls of 12 October.
entries.how: PUCL counted the electors left off the draft who are still on the State Election Commission's rolls, by the reason the Election Commission recorded and by district.
entries.access_text: The analysis, dated 11 November, reached the public through The Times of India.
entries.recorded: The State Election Commission's secretary told the paper that the state's roll numbers had increased in recent months and that the update process likely reduced the gap.

compare.what: The Election Commission's final roll, as PUCL gives it

entries.name: Karnataka's roll by religion, estimated
entries.covers: Karnataka's roll before the revision and its final roll, and the names left off the draft, divided by religion, and the booths that gave 60 per cent or more of their votes in the 2024 Lok Sabha election to the Congress.
entries.how: Sankalp, a political research consultancy in Karnataka, divided the figures by religion. The roll does not record religion, and Frontline says Sankalp's figures by religion are estimates.
entries.access_text: The estimates reached the public through Frontline.
